newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-CHAMPION BECKER DUMPED OUT OF AUSTRALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHAMPION BECKER DUMPED OUT OF AUSTRALIAN OPEN.

text.p: Defending champion Boris Becker tumbled out of the Australian Open on Monday, losing to Spain's Carlos Moya in a sensational first-round upset.
Moya, a clay court specialist world ranked 25th, beat the German world number six 5-7 7-6 (7-4) 3-6 6-1 6-4.
After a shaky start against Moya, who also beat him at the Paris Open last October, Becker appeared to have the match in his grasp as he built up a two sets to one lead.
But Moya replied with a succession of blistering passing shots, lightning service returns and clever lobs which left Becker cursing with frustration.
It is not the first time that two-time champion Becker has been an early loser at the year's first grand slam.
After winning the tournament in 1991, he was knocked out in the third round the following year and in the first round of the 1993 and 1995 tournaments.
But tour officials said he was the only defending men's champion in professional tennis history to lose in the first round of a grand slam event.
Becker's game was erratic throughout the three hours and 31 minutes of Monday's match. He served almost as many double faults as aces and failed to show his normal mastery at the net.
The German, who has won six grand slam events in his career, had been seen as the player most capable of beating world number one and top seed Pete Sampras.
His defeat will come as a boost to American Michael Chang, whom he would have met in the semifinals.
Becker beat Chang in last year's final.
Other matches on Monday's first day of action passed off with no major upsets.
Chang and women's world number one Steffi Graf cruised through to the second round -- although both had to do a spot of amateur nursing along the way.
Graf was leading 5-1 against Janette Husarova when the young Slovakian collapsed on centre court with a knee injury 22 minutes into their match.

Husarova was forced to wait several minutes before receiving treatment and top seed Graf, who won the match by default, was forced to step in and take a handful of ice cubes to ease her opponent's pain.
Chang also did some first aid during his 6-0 6-3 6-1 routing of Belgian qualifier Kris Goossens, handing a cold towel to a ball girl who fainted in the heat.
The American, who is seeking to win his first grand slam since capturing the French Open as a 17-year-old in 1989, was pleased with his game.

"It is always good to get off to a good start in the early rounds when the top players can falter a bit here in the first tournament of the year and get some nerves out of the system," he told reporters.

Becker's defeat will come as a major blow to tournament organisers, who have already lost some of the game's biggest names due to injury, most notably 1996 women's champion Monica Seles with a broken finger.

World men's number four Yevgeny Kafelnikov withdrew last week after breaking his hand and local star Mark Philippoussis, who ousted Sampras from the tournament last year, pulled out on Sunday because of tendinitis.

In other action on Monday, 15th seed Michael Stich saw off Sweden's Patrik Fredriksson 6-3 6-2 6-2 and women's third seed Conchita Martinez of Spain enjoyed a 6-0 6-2 win over Miriam Oremans of the Netherlands.
The youngest woman in the draw, 15-year-old Russian Anna Kournikova, made an early exit, losing 6-2 6-2 to 12th seed Amanda Coetzer of South Africa.
